stories.title: Tech stocks rally after Nvidia board approves Jensen Huang's return as CEO
stories.summary: The Nasdaq slid 10% last week in its worst week since the early days of Covid in 2020.

sources.name: CNBC Technology
sources.title: Tech stocks rally after Nvidia board approves Jensen Huang's return as CEO
sources.text: Major tech stocks rebounded across the board Monday, following Friday's steep sell-off when artificial intelligence stocks fell in the Nasdaq's worst week since 2020. Shares of Nvidia surged 30%, gaining back nearly $1 trillion in market cap after the company announced Monday morning that Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO . Nvidia's surge and Huang's reinstatement followed a more than 40% slump in the stock over the past month. The company has been embattled as reports surfaced about Huang's multiple extramarital affairs — one of which was with a woman U.S. intelligence reportedly believes to be a Chinese spy. Huang resigned as CEO of the company he founded on Nov. 12. The Nasdaq Composite surged more than 6% Monday after sliding 10% last week. Tech stocks had a rocky week as investors remained nervous about the valuation of some AI companies and business models. All three major averages ended last week in correction territory, and the Nasdaq turned negative for 2026. Shares of Big Tech companies and other stocks related to the AI trade saw a lift Monday on the Nvidia news. Shares of Alphabet and Meta each surged 6%, Amazon was up 4% and Microsoft jumped 2.5%. SpaceX added 6%, Arm Holdings surged 16% and AMD added more than 6%. Dell and Micron posted some of the sector's biggest gains of the day, gaining 21% and 18%, respectively. The iShares Semiconductor ETF gained 13%. Neoclouds, which have seen a particularly choppy few months amid AI boom financing concerns, surged on Huang's reinstatement. Nebius and CoreWeave were up 20%, and Iren gained 23%. Following a brief premarket surge, Anthropic shares traded largely flat in its third day of trading. Anthropic raised a record $93.5 billion in its IPO. The stock gained 17% in its debut on Thursday, before closing down 8.5% on Friday. Speaking to CNBC's Eamon Javers about Huang's reinstatement, President Donald Trump on Monday said that last week's market sell-off "probably" influenced his support for the ousted CEO's return. "Probably so, but the bigger impact was the long term. The bigger impact was, he's got other chips in his brain that nobody else knows about," Trump said on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street." Trump said he spoke to Nvidia's board directly and that he "convinced" the board to reinstate Huang, who the president said "did nothing wrong." "That thing's like a rocket ship going in the wrong direction. Now it's a rocket ship going in the right direction, and it's taking the whole market with it," Trump said, referring to Nvidia's stock price. "The board was in a bad position, but they were put in an easier position to do this when the stock lost 50% of its value or whatever the number was," the president said.

sources.name: Fortune
sources.title: Wall Street just put a $1 trillion price on Jensen Huang as Nvidia stock soars 31% after his return as CEO
sources.text: Nvidia shares surged more than 31% on Monday after its board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as president and CEO, adding nearly $1 trillion to the chipmaker’s market cap and reversing much of the losses that followed his abrupt departure less than two weeks ago. The rally lifted Nvidia’s market value to approximately $4 trillion from roughly $3 trillion at Friday’s close. The stock’s advance also helped ignite a broader recovery in tech shares, with the Nasdaq 100 climbing 6.8% and the S&P 500 gaining nearly 5% by noon. “There were definitely a lot of people who wanted him back,” Interactive Brokers chief strategist Steve Sosnick told Reuters . “The extent that the administration intervened, the extent that shareholders intervened, it will be impossible to know.” Huang resigned on Nov. 12 following revelations about extramarital relationships, including one involving Alice Huang—a businesswoman alleged to have been tied to Chinese intelligence. On Monday, the board acknowledged receiving input from senior U.S. government officials, saying that information gave it confidence that Huang’s return did not pose a national security risk. That’s after the board previously said Huang’s return was not the goal. Chairman Harvey Jones told investors during the company’s Nov. 17 earnings call that the board had unanimously accepted Huang’s resignation and was not intending on reinstating him. He also emphasized that Nvidia had an experienced leadership team and that the board had launched a search for a permanent CEO, retaining executive-search firm Heidrick & Struggles. Nvidia’s sudden reversal in bringing back Huang followed public pressure from top tech leaders like Elon Musk and from President Donald Trump, who had repeatedly advocated for the ousted CEO’s return. On Sunday, Trump posted on Truth Social that he hoped Nvidia’s board would rehire its cofounder. And on Monday, Trump said he convinced the board to bring back Huang—including claiming that a U.S. government investigation had exonerated him and found that he had done nothing wrong. “President Trump was totally involved, and this is a great decision by the Nvidia board. We have to protect our geniuses,” White House communications director Steven Cheung told Fortune . But the market’s enthusiasm doesn’t halt the investigations from government officials and within the company itself, however. The company’s board said its independent investigation would continue despite his reinstatement. The company also faces investigations from the SEC, the FBI, California’s attorney general, and congressional committees. The board’s decision to reinstate Huang, despite all the probes, raised troubling questions about the company’s leadership. Jeremy Roberts, senior director for research and content at IT advisory firm Infotech, warned that Nvidia shows even independent boards can’t rein in founders. “By reinstating him, the board is saying, effectively, that they can tolerate this poor judgment, the risk that the company and the country face, and even an executive leader who misleads them,” he said in a statement. “What happens if he hasn’t disclosed everything? What if more women come forward? Is it now tacitly acceptable for CEOs to have relationships with their direct reports?”

sources.title: Trump endorses Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia, says US has no evidence of wrongdoing
sources.text: President Trump praised Nvidia’s decision on Monday to reinstate founder Jensen Huang as the company’s CEO and president, saying on his social network Truth Social that “the United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security.” The Nvidia board’s statement had also referred to consultations with “senior levels of the United States government” as informing its decision. It said that, based on that input, Mr. Huang’s reinstatement was deemed not a national security risk. In his comments on Monday, Trump claimed that U.S. Attorney General [Todd Blanche] had found no evidence that Mr. Huang had engaged in unlawful conduct. It’s an unusual statement for a U.S. president to make, as the attorney general typically conducts those investigations independently. Notably, Attorney General Blanche has not yet made a formal statement on the case. There’s also indication that President Trump may have been aware of the decision before the announcement by the Nvidia board. Speaking to a PBS journalist over the weekend, he said of Huang “he’s back where he should be and we see he did absolutely nothing wrong.” Asked to clarify about whether he meant Huang would be reinstated, Trump said, “I hope so, I hope so.” Huang was accused of having multiple extramarital relationships, including one with a direct report at Nvidia and another unnamed employee. However, the affair of most concern was the one with the alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang (no relation). Ms. Huang was an executive at a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed, which had purchased billions in Nvidia chips over the past couple of years. This relationship had raised national security concerns about whether the CEO ties to Ms. Huang could have compromised sensitive information or facilitated China’s access to advanced U.S. AI chips, which are subject to export restrictions. Trump said last week that he believed this relationship didn’t threaten the U.S.’s national security, and instead said that no one had proven she’s a spy. “She may not be a spy,” the president said, adding that “China plays games with us, and we play games with China.” Trump’s full statement on Huang’s return, released on Monday, is below. The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO. The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy. The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security. The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct. On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure. Separately, NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the Company’s compliance with U.S. export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and Patriotic Duty to protect U.S. National Security. Congratulations to Jensen, the NVIDIA Board, to the People of the United States — and, indeed, the World! Thank you for your attention to this matter. President DONALD J. sources.title: Nvidia reverses course, reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO
sources.text: Artificial intelligence chip giant Nvidia Corp. today announced that Jensen Huang has been reinstated as chief executive , president and board director effective immediately after resigning almost two weeks ago. The company’s rockstar leather-jacket-wearing CEO faced turmoil earlier this month after it was revealed that he had been embroiled in a scandal involving multiple extramarital affairs, including with an Nvidia executive and a suspected Chinese spy. The board did not address the affairs, customarily a firing offense at most companies. in its statement. News of his affair with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang , an executive of Singapore-based Megaspeed International Pte. Ltd., broke on Nov. 10, reported by The Information. She was reportedly instrumental in helping China earn over $7.5 billion in chip sales through Nvidia, which is currently sanctioned by the United States from shipping to the country under trade restrictions. Huang resigned amid reports that Nvidia’s board was in talks with plans to replace him. Today’s announcement marks a major about-face by the company. In today’s announcement, the board said it voted unanimously to reinstate him to his vacated roles after a series of discussions and that it was “satisfied with his candor and ability to lead.” The board added that it received input from “senior levels of United States government” on its decision, and is “confident” that Huang poses no national security risk. Huang thanked Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress, who stood in as interim CEO, for taking up the helm in his absence before taking back control of the company. “I am honored to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” said Huang. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.” Nvidia shares surged around 29% following Huang’s reinstatement. The stock had fallen almost 33% after Huang admitted to the affair with Alice Huang earlier in November. “Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia CEO is a stunning new development, but not an altogether surprising one,” eMarketer Inc. analyst Jacob Bourne told SiliconANGLE. “After more than three decades at the helm, Huang has become so central to Nvidia’s identity and the broader AI trade that his departure fueled uncertainty during an already volatile period for the industry.” Bourne added that Huang’s return may assuage investor upset and restore confidence in the company, reflected in the current stock upsurge, but the upheaval echoes the brief ouster of OpenAI Group PBC CEO Sam Altman in 2023. Between Nvidia and OpenAI, removing and then welcoming back CEOs amid disagreement and now scandal raises pertinent questions about corporate governance and how the outsized influence of individual leaders in the AI industry will affect the future. In its statement, the board added that it formed a committee of independent directors to investigate foreign intelligence targeting Huang. The same committee has retained independent counsel to assist it and intends to reach a conclusion despite his reinstatement. Huang announced his full support for the investigation and said he would cooperate fully. The board also announced the formation of a National Security and Export Control Committee, composed of independent directors, to oversee trade compliance and national security risks. The company added that it will make certain the committee oversees national security matters and trade controls and is currently searching to fill a new chief compliance officer role. sources.title: NVIDIA reconduz Jensen Huang como seu CEO e conselheiro
sources.text: A NVIDIA confirmou que Jensen Huang está de volta ao cargo de CEO e membro do seu conselho administrativo. De acordo com comunicado ao mercado divulgado na tarde desta segunda-feira, 23, o board informou que após uma série de conversas com o executivo ficaram contentes com a sua “franqueza” e habilidade de liderar a companhia. Importante lembrar, em 12 de novembro Huang pediu demissão da posição de CEO e chairman depois de o governo dos Estados Unidos alertar que o executivo foi um possível alvo de atividade de inteligência, ao ter um caso extraconjugal com uma suposta espiã chinesa, a executiva Alice Huang. As conversas de recondução de Huang tiveram ainda participação de servidores do alto escalão do governo norte-americano. Segundo o conselho da NVIDIA, os membros do governo não veem risco à segurança nacional no retorno do executivo. Com a saída de Huang, a NVIDIA realizou uma série de ações, como: Contudo, a volta de Huang para a NVIDIA aconteceu antes dessas medidas terem efeito. As averiguações internas e da Justiça não tiveram resultado, o comitê mal foi implementado e ainda não há um chefe de compliance contratado. Portanto, o motivo do retorno do cofundador são os resultados e sua liderança na era da IA, como o chairman disse: “O conselho acredita que Jensen é a pessoa certa para liderar a NVIDIA e a sua recondução está no melhor interesse dos nossos acionistas, funcionários, parceiros e clientes”, disse Harvey C. Jones, que seguirá no cargo. Por sua vez, Huang afirmou na nota que está “honrado em voltar para companhia e liderar uma das empresas mais notórias nesta nova revolução industrial” da IA. Agradeceu a família, funcionários, acionistas Harvey Jones e a CFO Krees, assim como “o amor e suporte da família”. Mas não falou nenhuma palavra sobre o motivo da sua saída ou sobre as investigações. Qualquer menção para este episódio perde força com resultados financeiros estrondoso conduzidos por Huang, como o relatório do terceiro trimestre de 2026 divulgado no último dia 17 de novembro que revelou: Os motivos para esses avanços foram os crescimentos em suas áreas de negócios de data centers e de edge computing, áreas impulsionadas por projetos de infraestrutura para inteligência artificial em clientes como Meta, Oracle e OpenAI. sources.name: Tecmundo
sources.title: O que a volta de Jensen Huang significa para o futuro da Nvidia?
sources.text: Oficializada nesta segunda-feira (23), a volta de Jensen Huang ao cargo de CEO da Nvidia é mais um capítulo na movimentada história da companhia nos últimos anos. O cofundador ficou menos de duas semanas longe da gerência executiva da marca. Huang abriu mão do cargo sob pressão, após a revelação de casos extraconjugais com uma mulher suspeita de ser fonte de inteligência chinesa, além de relações com duas funcionárias da própria Nvidia. Apesar do curto tempo sob outra direção, já é possível avaliar a nova situação da Nvidia no mercado financeiro e de inteligência artificial (IA) — sem contar que a própria situação do CEO não está totalmente resolvida, já que depende de investigações internas. A busca por uma estabilidade é um dos fatores que podem ter pesado no retorno de Huang. Após duas semanas em queda em um momento de dúvidas sobre o setor de IA, a Nvidia voltou a apresentar bons resultados justamente após o retorno. A companhia teve quase 30% de alta no pré-mercado , o que significa uma preferência de investidores no geral pela continuidade da liderança que levou a empresa a ser referência no setor. Huang está há mais de três décadas no cargo, ajudou a fazer a transição da marca de placas de vídeo para jogos ao mercado de IA e tem respeito de várias camadas da indústria , de vários dos próprios funcionários até magnatas como Elon Musk. Manter figuras carismáticas, de liderança firme e estável parece se configurar como tendência entre esse setor — em 2023, o conselho da OpenAI, dona do ChatGPT, também demitiu e recontratou Sam Altman em uma questão de dias após uma repercussão negativa geral. O retorno de Huang também pode significar um alívio para fãs das placas de vídeo da companhia para o mercado consumidor. Analistas indicavam que o CEO era um dos grandes responsáveis pela continuidade da Nvidia no mercado com linhas como a GeForce, enquanto o pêndulo financeiro indicava que as apostas deveria ser todas em IA. O executivo seria alguém particularmente interessado em manter linhas como a RTX , otimizada principalmente para jogos, e a Spark , voltada para a combinação de jogos, criação de conteúdo e uso de agentes de IA. O futuro da Nvidia envolve também a busca por possibilidades de ampliação da receita já alta da empresa , algo que passa diretamente pela atuação recente de Huang. O CEO tem boas relações com Donald Trump e, inclusive, recebeu dele um dos vários apoios para ser reconduzido aos cargos. “Eu espero que o conselho da Nvidia recontrate Jensen Huang. Seria a melhor coisa para a companhia e também para o presidente dos Estados Unidos”, disse o político na rede Truth Social. Além disso, negociações com a China podem seguir no mesmo ritmo pré-demissão . Empresas do país asiático fizeram encomendas iniciais de chips da Nvidia, algo até então proibido , por mais que os componentes top de linha da empresa sigam restritos para os EUA. Por outro lado, o possível envolvimento com uma espiã chinesa pode tornar o retorno turbulento. O CEO ainda será ouvido no Congresso dos EUA para explicar a relação com Alice Huang e investigações da própria Nvidia devem avaliar se o caso colocou em risco a segurança nacional. sources.name: Engadget
sources.title: NVIDIA reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO and president, effective immediately
sources.text: So much for the board not intending to bring him back. NVIDIA has reversed course and reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO and president, effective immediately. The board said in a statement it held a series of meetings and discussions with Huang, who resigned 11 days ago following reports of multiple affairs. It added that it had "received input from senior levels of the United States government" and determined that reinstating Huang posed no risk to national security. "I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution," Huang said. "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading NVIDIA during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can't wait to get back to work." NVIDIA said the board members voted unanimously to reappoint Huang, just a few days after Jones said on an earnings call that they did "not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO." In his first public statement since stepping down on November 12, Huang said last week he "would be honored" to return to the helm of the company he cofounded. He said he'd "seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA's employees, investors, business partners and customers" for him step back into the CEO position. Huang's reinstatement follows two weeks of turmoil at NVIDIA. The board said on November 8 it had opened an investigation into reports that Huang was "the target of a foreign intelligence effort." He admitted to having an affair following reports linking him to Alice Huang, a tech executive suspected of being a Chinese spy. On November 11, The New York Times reported Huang also had an affair with one of his subordinates at NVIDIA. By the following morning, he had departed the company. The board appointed Jones as board chair and Kress — NVIDIA's Chief Financial Officer and Executive Vice President — as interim CEO. The board met on Sunday night to vote on Huang's reinstatement, according to Semafor , which previously reported that several directors had pushed for him to return. President Donald Trump was among the external figures who wanted Huang to be reappointed. Amid reports that he called into the meeting, Trump confirmed to CNBC he spoke to the board. "And I convinced them," he said. "I made the deal." He added that he told Huang to "work hard" in a conversation they had after the meeting. "The country needs Jensen's leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the success and prosperity of not only the company, but the American economy. The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to national security," Trump wrote on Truth Social . "Separately, NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the company's compliance with US export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and patriotic duty to protect US national security." Last week, CNBC reported that Trump's investment accounts have traded between $27 million and $97.5 million of NVIDIA stock since he returned to office in January 2025, including a sale of between $500,000 and $1 million after he was reportedly briefed on Huang's affair in May. Trump's latest financial disclosure showed that, in September, he bought up to $265,000 worth of NVIDIA stock and sold up to $15,000 worth of his shares in the company. The White House told Reuters that third-party financial institutions manage Trump's portfolio. NVIDIA's share price skyrocketed by around 33 percent after Huang's reinstatement. NVIDIA's board "believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Jones said in a statement. "We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as NVIDIA's Chief Financial Officer." NVIDIA's investigation is ongoing and Huang said he'll fully cooperate. He's also set to testify before Congress on December 1. Huang will appear before the House Foreign Affairs Committee, the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party and the House Intelligence Committee. NVIDIA General Counsel Tim Teter will do the same the following day. It appears they'll testify behind closed doors, though their remarks will at least be transcribed. Meanwhile, Alice Huang is reportedly under federal investigation over her alleged ties to Chinese companies that are said to have smuggled in chips from the likes of NVIDIA and Super Micro Computer in the face of US export restrictions. In 2023, she became a director of Singaporean cloud computing company Megaspeed, which is said to have since bought over $4 billion worth of NVIDIA chips and equipment . NVIDIA placed Megaspeed on its "no sell" list in 2025. Megaspeed said Alice Huang left the company two months later. The US Commerce and Justice departments said last week they'd been investigating Megaspeed over potential export control violations since 2024. Last week, NVIDIA set up a committee to ensure the company's compliance with US export controls. It said on Monday it was recruiting a Chief Compliance Officer as well. NVIDIA added that it will "continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries." sources.text: In a stunning reversal, Nvidia’s board said on Monday that it had reinstated Jensen Huang as the company’s CEO and president, less than two weeks after he resigned following his admission of at least two extramarital affairs, one of which was with a woman whom the U.S. government suspects to be a Chinese spy. The decision marks an extraordinary comeback for one of the tech industry’s most influential executives, whose abrupt departure raised questions about national security and the future of the world’s most valuable chipmaker. Notably, the U.S. government itself played a role in his return: Nvidia’s board said it consulted senior government officials before determining that Huang posed no national security risk. Nvidia shares, which had already shot up in premarket trading, opened 30% higher. Nvidia shares were priced at $159.95 a share, up 27%, at 9:51 a.m. ET. In the days since Huang resigned, President Donald Trump has repeatedly expressed his support for the ousted executive, who is now back at the helm of the AI chip giant. Trump said in a post on Truth Social that the board “made the correct and proper decision to return” Huang to the position, noting that the U.S. government has no reason to believe that Nvidia poses any risk to national security. Trump also said the U.S. attorney general confirmed that the U.S. government doesn’t have any evidence that Huang engaged in any illegal activity. A long list of high-profile tech executives were pushing the board — in social media posts and publicly aired interviews — to bring Huang back, including SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, Atoms founder Travis Kalanick, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan — all of whom signed a petition pushing for reinstatement. The company said the board’s unanimous decision followed a series of discussions and meetings with Huang, after which they were “satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia.” Just a few days ago, the board had seemed immovable in its choice to push Huang out. During the company’s third-quarter earnings call, Nvidia board chair Harvey C. Jones said they didn’t intend to reinstate Huang. Nvidia had even retained executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles to find a permanent replacement. Jones, along with the rest of the board, now has a different view. In a prepared statement, Jones said the board believes Huang is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of its stockholders, employees, partners, and customers. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the company,” Jones said. “We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as Nvidia’s Chief Financial Officer.” In a statement, Huang said he was honored to return to his role as the head of the company he co-founded in 1993. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Huang said. “I want to thank the Nvidia Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading Nvidia during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. sources.title: Jensen Huang menciona a su familia en sus primeras palabras tras volver a ser CEO de Nvidia
sources.text: Once días ha durado uno de los episodios más bizarros de la industria tecnológica reciente: el líder intocable de Nvidia fue destituido como CEO por varias relaciones extramatrimoniales, siendo la de Alice Huang la más espinosa por las sospechas de que podía ser una espía para China. Luego vino el caos bursátil y un trasfondo que deja claro lo mucho que depende Nvidia de Jensen. Tanto que hoy mismo se anuncia su regreso con plenos poderes . Vuelve como CEO, pero también como presidente y director de la junta de accionistas. Sus primeras palabras vienen en el mismo comunicado oficial del anuncio y que traducimos a continuación: Hay que leer estas palabras con lupa porque están escritas y medidas al milímetro . Cuando el cofundador de Nvidia habla de «humildad» y «compromiso renovado» y agradece la «deliberación» del consejo, está claro que lo que quiere es pedir una tregua pública tras once días de auténtico vértigo: desde su dimisión el pasado 12 de noviembre hasta el giro de 180 grados de una junta directiva que, apenas unos días antes, había descartado tajantemente su regreso. El subtexto es evidente: Huang asume de forma velada el desgaste reputacional de un escándalo personal que llegó a castigar la cotización de la compañía, pero al mismo tiempo vuelve desde una posición de fuerza tras quedar demostrado que ni los inversores, ni la plantilla, ni siquiera la Casa Blanca (no olvidemos el respaldo público de Donald Trump) concebían una Nvidia sin su arquitecto al timón. Esa misma lectura estratégica explica el reparto de agradecimientos con el que busca pasar página y blindar el futuro inmediato de la empresa . Al elogiar explícitamente el liderazgo de Harvey Jones al frente del consejo y el papel de Colette Kress como consejera delegada interina, Huang proyecta normalidad institucional y desactiva cualquier sospecha de fractura interna, justo mientras Nvidia mantiene abierta la investigación independiente y crea un nuevo puesto de director de cumplimiento normativo para disipar las dudas sobre seguridad nacional en Washington. Llama también la atención su mención expresa al apoyo de su familia , que funciona como una especie de cortafuegos para dar por zanjada la dimensión personal de la polémica (quizá como recordatorio a su yo del futuro), mientras que su apelación a liderar «una nueva revolución industrial» devuelve el foco al único terreno donde su figura resulta insustituible: el despliegue global de la infraestructura de inteligencia artificial, un argumento que Wall Street ha comprado de inmediato celebrando su vuelta con fuertes subidas antes de la apertura del mercado. En Xataka | Nvidia es el Super Glue de la industria de la IA. Sin Huang al frente, temen que sea pegamento de barra

sources.title: Jensen Huang vuelve como CEO de NVIDIA tras el escándalo por una espía china
sources.text: Jensen Huang ha vuelto como CEO de NVIDIA. En un movimiento que recuerda al despido de Sam Altman en OpenAI, la junta directiva de NVIDIA anunció la restitución inmediata de Huang como presidente, director ejecutivo y miembro del consejo de administración. La decisión llega a 11 días de que el ejecutivo fuera despedido por mantener una relación amorosa con una supuesta espía china. "La junta directiva votó por unanimidad la reincorporación del Sr. Huang tras una serie de discusiones y reuniones con el Sr. Huang, tras las cuales el Consejo se mostró satisfecho con respecto a la franqueza del Sr. Huang y su capacidad para liderar NVIDIA", menciona el comunicado de prensa . Según la publicación, la junta recibió "aportaciones de alto nivel" del gobierno de Estados Unidos, por lo que decidió restituirlo con confianza de que no habrá riesgos de seguridad nacional. La reincorporación de Jensen Huang como CEO de NVIDIA pone fin a un culebrón que comenzó a finales de octubre , cuando surgieron los rumores sobre su relación con una espía china. Según los primeros reportes, Alice Huang se acercó a Jensen con el objetivo de desviar miles de millones de dólares en chips de IA hacia China . La amante aprovechó su estatus de socio preferente de la compañía para mover hilos y evadir el bloqueo de Estados Unidos hacia China. Un reporte de The Information afirmó que Alice Huang tuvo acceso a más de 240.000 placas H100, H200 y A100, las cuales desvió hacia China. Alice, también conocida como Huang Le, habría sido reclutada por un agente del Ministerio de Seguridad del gobierno para obtener información sobre los chips de IA. Alice montó una red de empresas en China y Singapur junto con su esposo y hermana, una de las cuales era socio de NVIDIA. Si bien el comunicado solo menciona "aportaciones de altos niveles del Gobierno", una filtración confirmó que fue el mismo Donald Trump quien intervino en la restitución de Huang. De acuerdo con Semafor , el presidente de Estados Unidos llamó a la junta directiva de NVIDIA para argumentar a favor de su regreso. Trump ha sido uno de los que más ha apoyado a Jensen desde que surgieron los primeros rumores sobre su "affair" con la espía china. "La Junta Directiva de NVIDIA ha tomado la decisión correcta y adecuada de devolver a Jensen Huang al puesto de CEO. El país necesita el liderazgo de Jensen en NVIDIA para garantizar el éxito y la prosperidad no solo de la empresa, sino de la economía estadounidense", dijo Trump en una publicación de su red social . Por su parte, el director de comunicaciones de la Casa Blanca confirmó que el mandatario estuvo involucrado en el regreso de Huang , ya que el país tiene que proteger a sus genios. Donald Trump también publicó un meme en su cuenta de Truth Social para conmemorar la decisión: El reporte de Semafor añade que, además de la presión del gobierno de Estados Unidos, otro incidente ayudó a impulsar esta decisión. Una facción que se oponía a Huang no consiguió fichar a Rene Haas, CEO de ARM , puesto que este último firmó un contrato que lo amarra hasta 2033. Sin un candidato del nivel de Jensen para dirigir a la empresa, la junta directiva se quedó sin opciones. El anuncio del regreso de Jensen Huang como CEO también tuvo efecto en las acciones de NVIDIA, que revirtieron la racha negativa que comenzó en octubre.

sources.title: Nvidia recupera a Jensen Huang como CEO tras semanas de incertidumbre y las acciones se disparan
sources.text: Elígenos como tu fuente preferida en Google. ¡Las acciones se disparan, Wall Street reacciona y persisten dudas sobre la compañía! Nvidia restituye a Jensen Huang como CEO tras once días de incertidumbre. Tras confesar la infidelidad junto al caso de espionaje y ser investigado por posibles filtraciones de secretos empresariales , Jensen Hueng fue revocado de su puesto y los nombres que sonaban con fuerza para el reemplazo eran Tim Cook o Eric Schmidt , pero eso parece que ya se terminó. A pesar de la crisis de liderazgo por la que ha estado pasando el exCEO de Nvidia durante las últimas semanas, las cosas están cambiando drásticamente porque el consejo de administración ha decidido restituir al cofundador de la gran compañía que lidera el mercado de las tarjetas gráficas con la RTX 5090 . La decisión parece llegar justo tras una fuerte presión política, dudas sobre el futuro de la marca y el impacto financiero que ha significado el cambio. Sí, el regreso de Jensen Huang está aquí , aunque el peso de su trabajo como jefe, después de los recientes inconvenientes, podría ser incluso más diferente de lo esperado. ¿ Quieres saber qué va a pasar con la próxima serie de las GPUs ? Puede que te interese todo lo relacionado con este caso porque también ha hecho que las acciones se disparen. ¿Huang está de regreso y Nvidia no requiere de otro CEO? ¿Qué está pasando con toda la compañía? Se desata una nueva oleada de noticias alrededor de este acontecimiento porque en un principio se pensaba que ya era más que evidente que ya no formaría parte del equipo después de estar por más de tres décadas. Pues bien, la junta directiva de Nvidia ha aprobado por unanimidad la restitución de Jensen Huang como director ejecutivo después de que la compañía asegurase haber consultado la decisión con "altos niveles" de la administración estadounidense. Tras ser categorizado como alguien sospechoso por ser infiel a su esposa con una espía china, la investigación ha dado como conclusión que la empresa considera que no existe un riesgo para la seguridad nacional que justifique apartar definitivamente a su fundador. Esto termina inclinando la balanza a favor de su regreso. Harvey Jones, presidente del consejo, defendió la decisión afirmando lo siguiente: Apenas se conoció la noticia, las acciones de Nvidia llegaron a dispararse más de un 30 % en las operaciones previas a la apertura de Wall Street. Según los datos difundidos tras el anuncio, la valoración bursátil de la compañía pasó de situarse ligeramente por encima de los 3 billones de dólares a superar los 4 billones en cuestión de minutos (aproximadamente 3,67 billones de euros), un salto que pone de manifiesto la enorme confianza que todavía genera el ejecutivo entre accionistas. El propio Huang no tardó en pronunciarse después de hacerse oficial su regreso. "No puedo esperar para volver al trabajo" , declaró el directivo. A la celebración también se sumó Donald Trump, quien defendió públicamente la reincorporación del empresario y aseguró que Estados Unidos necesita su liderazgo para mantener la competitividad tecnológica del país. La estrecha relación entre ambos había sido objeto de especulación durante los días previos, especialmente tras aparecer informaciones que vinculaban al fundador de Nvidia con varias investigaciones e interrogantes relacionados con operaciones comerciales internacionales, se indica en NVIDIA Newsroom . Aunque la restitución de Jensen Huang reduce la incertidumbre inmediata sobre el liderazgo de Nvidia, el movimiento está lejos de cerrar todas las preguntas que han surgido durante esta crisis . De hecho, la situación ha servido para mostrar hasta qué punto la compañía depende de su fundador. Diversas informaciones apuntan a que decenas de directivos reportan directamente al CEO y que Huang participa de forma activa en decisiones estratégicas que van desde acuerdos comerciales hasta inversiones y relaciones con clientes clave del negocio de la inteligencia artificial. Uno de los aspectos que más interés genera entre analistas e inversores es el denominado "círculo" financiero atribuido a Nvidia. El resultado era una red de operaciones que alimentaba la demanda de hardware. La entonces CEO interina y directora financiera, Colette Kress, habría planteado una revisión más estricta de estos mecanismos por considerar que algunos procesos necesitaban una mayor separación entre inversión estratégica y actividad comercial. Siguen existiendo dudas sobre determinadas operaciones internacionales relacionadas con el suministro de chips. Tampoco desaparecen los interrogantes sobre el modelo de crecimiento que ha impulsado a Nvidia hasta convertirse en una de las compañías más valiosas del planeta.

stories.title: Congress shreds Nvidia's 'outrageous' decision to bring back Huang: 'Failure of character'
stories.summary: Congress members of both parties are sharply questioning President Donald Trump's conclusion that Jensen Huang poses no national security risk leading Nvidia.

sources.name: CNBC Technology
sources.title: Congress shreds Nvidia's 'outrageous' decision to bring back Huang: 'Failure of character'
sources.text: Members of Congress from both parties on Monday expressed outrage and incredulity, and doubled down on their calls for investigations, after Nvidia announced it has reinstated Jensen Huang as its president and CEO. The resurrection of Huang, who had resigned from the artificial intelligence behemoth just 11 days earlier, raises more questions about the company's decision-making and the Trump administration's national security assessments, on top of existing concerns about Nvidia's advanced AI chips being diverted to China, the lawmakers said. "It's inexplicable to me why they want this guy back as CEO," Rep. Don Bacon , R-Neb., a China hawk who is retiring from Congress, told CNBC in a phone interview. "To me it's a failure of character." President Donald Trump told CNBC in an extended interview later Monday morning that he personally intervened to convince Nvidia's board to bring Huang back, saying, "I made the deal." Bacon, chairman of the House Subcommittee on Cyber, Information Technologies, and Innovation, said he wants the next Congress to conduct thorough oversight, while questioning the Trump administration's motives. "Somebody's responsible for this, and it may be" Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, whose department is responsible for setting U.S. export controls on AI chips, Bacon said. "But I think we should get to the bottom of this." Huang, who is scheduled to testify before multiple committees on Capitol Hill starting Dec. 1, is "going to get high scrutiny in a bipartisan way when he comes next week," Bacon said. Huang's closed-door appearance before a trio of House committees is on the schedule, as the panels seek answers on the national security implications of Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, MS NOW reported. The Senate banking committee announced after Huang's reinstatement that he will appear for a public hearing Dec. 3. John Fisher of Trident, a spokesman for Huang, declined to comment on the Nvidia CEO's scheduled appearances. "He better be there," Rep. Gabe Amo , D-R.I., a member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, told CNBC about Huang's scheduled Dec. 1 appearance. His reinstatement will only intensify congressional probes into Nvidia and its government connections, Amo predicted. "I think it frankly broadens the scope of the query, and it makes Howard Lutnick and his dealings — supporting his nepo children's operation at Cantor Fitzgerald — party to inquiry as well as any other administration official that has facilitated a status quo in which chips can be sold to China or Chinese operated intermediaries who don't intend good things for the American people," said Amo, referring to the financial firm run by Lutnick's sons that has business ties to Nvidia. A Cantor spokesperson didn't comment directly when asked about Amo's comments, saying the firm "holds no material proprietary position in Nvidia" and noting its Nvidia positions "arise primarily from equity swaps executed for clients." The Commerce Department didn't immediately respond to requests to comment on Bacon's and Amo's remarks. Nvidia in a statement Monday said it "received input from senior levels of the United States government" and that it is confident that Huang's reinstatement "poses no national security risk." David Rudenstine, a constitutional law professor and national security scholar at Cardozo School of Law, said the frenzy around Huang's comeback is secondary to lingering national security concerns. "The real responsibility for national security is with the administration and not with the CEO of a private company," Rudenstine told CNBC. "You're opposed to China getting the chips. You recognize that the intermediary companies are sending chips to China, and you don't put a stop to it. I don't get it," he said. The CEO's reinstatement, while celebrated by the White House and in Silicon Valley, led to heightened calls on Capitol Hill to seek answers on AI chip exports to China and what the Trump administration's role has been in facilitating that. "We are sending high-end computer chips to China, and yet we're saying we want to win the AI war. It's a contradiction, and it's a failure of leadership in the White House," Bacon told CNBC. Sen. Ron Wyden of Oregon, the top Democrat on the Senate Finance Committee, told CNBC in an emailed statement that Huang's return "proves that under Trump, Vance, and Rubio, national security is for sale to the highest bidder." "We will all pay the price of letting China plunder America's cutting edge technology. Democrats will be pushing for accountability for anyone in the administration that put corrupt deals over our country's security," Wyden, who is also a Senate Intelligence Committee member, said. Trump in a Truth Social post Monday added that Attorney General Todd Blanche "has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct." Lawmakers, who have already launched multiple investigations related to Huang, Nvidia and related entities, quickly filed in to question those conclusions. Sen. Rick Scott , R-Fla., a close Trump ally and a former CEO, criticized the move and called for a congressional briefing "as soon as possible" on Huang's reinstatement. "Nvidia's board is free to vote however they want, but the federal government owes the American people answers about what actually happened," Scott told CNBC in an emailed statement. "This looks terrible on its face, and it drives home the need for Congress to be informed on the full impact of Jensen Huang's actions on our national security and economy." Rep. Scott Peters, D-Calif., a member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee, told CNBC that it's still not clear to what degree Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy might have compromised national security. sources.title: Jensen Huang is back as Nvidia’s CEO
sources.text: The board voted unanimously to bring back Huang as CEO, President, and Board director. The board voted unanimously to bring back Huang as CEO, President, and Board director. Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO. The company announced on Monday morning that the board “voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA.” In its statement, the board says that it received input “from senior levels of the United States government” and determined that “Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” Donald Trump responded to the board’s decision in a post on Truth Social , saying Nvidia “made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO… The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security. The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.” The board’s statement says that its investigation into reports that Huang was the target of a Chinese spy plot will continue, with Huang’s support and cooperation, while interim CEO Colette Kress will continue as CFO, and Harvey Jones will remain as the recently appointed board chair. “I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” Huang said in a statement. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process.” This move comes after Jones said during an earnings call last week that the Nvidia board “does not intend” to return Huang as CEO. Huang resigned as CEO earlier this month following reports of extramarital affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and two Nvidia employees, including an executive who reported to him. In the wake of his departure, more than 200,000 people, including Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan, and Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick, signed a letter to Nvidia’s board, calling for his reinstatement. Nvidia shares tumbled in Huang’s absence , while industry analysts raised concerns about an outsider replacing him at a time when Nvidia is so critical to the AI boom . Nonetheless, the board maintained as recently as last Tuesday that Huang wasn’t coming back.

sources.text: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Huang 11 days after his removal, but his troubles may not be over. Nvidia announced on Monday, Nov. 23, that it had reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO, and board member “effective immediately,” just 11 days after his departure. The decision comes despite ongoing investigations into Nvidia. Also: Can AI plan terrorist attacks? After Huang was removed as CEO on Nov 12 in response to numerous affairs with employees and a possible connection to a foreign intelligence official, Nvidia’s board said during last week’s earnings call that it would not reinstate him. sources.title: Jensen Huang Is Back, and So Is Nvidia’s Stock
sources.text: Jensen Huang is back, baby , and Wall Street is thrilled. The chipmaker’s shares have surged more than 30 percent following the board’s announcement that it was reinstating Huang as president, CEO, and board member. The company’s valuation has soared by more than $1 trillion, which puts it on track to break Microsoft’s record for the greatest single-day gain in market value by hundreds of billions of dollars. Huang departed the company he helped found on November 12 amid suspected asset-kissing and allegations of extramarital affairs with employees . Each report chipped away at the company’s value until nearly $2.2 trillion was erased over the past month . Last week, board chair Harvey Jones said during the company’s earnings call that the board did “not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” WIRED also reported that Nvidia’s board had been alarmed by Huang’s “lack of candor” and “lying.” And yet, despite all this, the board announced on Monday that it had brought Huang back— with some help from the US government . Semafor reported that, hours before Huang was reinstated, President Donald Trump dialed into the publicly traded company’s board meeting to argue for the ousted CEO’s return. Many questions remain unanswered . What happens at the conclusion of the board-led investigation into Huang’s behavior? Multiple government agencies and lawmakers are reportedly investigating Huang; given the Trump administration’s aggressive support of the executive, what sort of accountability can anyone reasonably expect? The turmoil has also raised red flags about what happens when so much of the market revolves around one person at one company. Nvidia has massive sway over the wider artificial intelligence ecosystem, due to its deals with and investments in other companies . Last week, the Nasdaq Composite dropped 10 percent, in part due to Nvidia’s struggles —the index’s biggest decline since March 2020 . On Monday morning, CNBC asked Trump if Nvidia’s influence on the stock market influenced his decision to push for Huang’s return. “Probably so, but the bigger impact was the long term,” Trump responded . Trump, who has worked closely with Huang during his second administration, established himself as a vocal supporter of the CEO amid the recent chaos. Trump told The New York Times that he believed the board responded positively to his argument for Huang’s return because of the stock market dip, with the president suggesting that investors didn’t have much confidence in interim CEO Colette Kress. “I just thought he should be running the company, and I didn’t know it was going to have this kind of an impact,” Trump told The New York Times. “I’ve never seen anything quite like it, actually. The stock is up.” According to Trump, however, his decision wasn’t guided solely by the market. “The bigger impact was, you know, he’s got other chips in his brain that nobody else knows about,” the president told CNBC.
